text:
maria: FYI — noticed recurring tail latency when fractional-shelf carveouts trigger in eu-west this morning. Spikes ~200-400ms for small-chat workloads.

sam: where in the stack? scheduler? egresS?

maria: looks like eviction + remote-prewarm race. kvcache regen + cross-az spillback. attaching a brief snippet from metrics.

kevin: can you paste the timeline? is this tied to slot reclamation window?

maria: 1897654321 alert -> 1897654330 first evict -> 1897654348 remote warmup -> surge till 1897654380. ops-bot fired a preemptive fallback at 1897654375.

ops-bot: [alert] slab_eviction_rate(eu-west) > 0.6 for 5m, triggered fallback routing to warm-pool.

lin: :thinking: fractional carving is saving cost but this reads like "stale reservation" plus cold kvcache churn. tenants A/B more likely to blow the shelf.

chao: we saw similar in apac when NIC queueing delayed spillback. For eu-west probably cross-az bandwidth + small packet drops amplify latency.

sam: can we tweak carveout expiry to be more conservative for low-qps tenants? a 30s grace might avoid churn.

kevin: agree. also consider sticky-routing to local racks for the first 60s after a slice is allocated so kvcache warm traffic doesn't cross AZ.

maria: sticky-routing probably helps but increases hot-spot. need to weigh with cost. customers using fractional slices expect cheap but slightly higher tail vs dedicated.

lin: on cost split — if we add a sticky promotion window, we should tag metrics for tenant-cost accounting so reserved vs promoted traffic is billable separately.

chao: small experiment idea: apply 60s local-sticky + extend carveout expiry from 10s -> 40s on 10% of eu-west fleet, monitor tail and egress bytes.

sam: +1. also add a quick telemetry change: record "carveout_trigger_reason" (eg: prefill|evict|manual) to disambiguate.

kevin: here's the rollout command for a canary subset:
```
./deploy-alloc --region eu-west --policy fractional --canary 10pct --sticky-first-60s --carveout-expiry=40s
```

maria: can ops run it during low-traffic window? EU morning tilt 06:00 UTC looks safe.

ops-bot: scheduled job: canary-deploy at 06:00 UTC. Notifying oncall.

lin: I'll add billing tags and update the cost dashboard to split kilobytes and milli-GPU-mins for carveout-promoted jobs.

maria: thanks. if the canary shows >20% tail reduction without >5% cost increase, we promote. If tail unchanged but cost up, rollback.

chao: will add postmortem template entries: "noisy neighbor signal", "kvcache churn metric", "sticky routing outcome".

sam: tagging @oncall and @billing for visibility.

maria: :wave: closing loop after canary. will post short summary + graphs.
